name: Figure_1
caption: Figure 1. Animal-level design and aggregate junction differences. a) RR23 cerebellar source animals and collection dates; technical libraries are not biological replicates. b) Principal components of all 5,249 measured binary choices, centered across 26 animals without selection by test results. c) All animal retained unique-junction depths; segments show group means. d) RMS differences in group mean fractions over the same 5,249 choices. Exact whole-animal allocations enumerate 48,620 FLT–GC and 24,310 assignments in each 9-versus-8 comparison, with Holm correction across three global tests. These are effect summaries, not bars hiding biological variation; the animal distributions appear in b and c. FLT, flight; GC, habitat ground control; VIV, vivarium control. FLT n=9, GC n=9, VIV n=8. Collection-date aliasing limits causal interpretation.

name: Figure_2
caption: Figure 2. Conservative gene localization and animal-level measurements. a) Every measured gene in the FLT–GC comparison; blue points pass joint Benjamini–Yekutieli correction across 5,949 gene–contrast tests. All 47 calls have exact p=2/48,620 and q=0.04825699; the dashed line is q=0.05. b,c) Every measured choice and all animals for post hoc illustrative genes Hnrnpa2b1 and Stxbp1. Each dot is one animal and each segment a group mean; FLT n=9, GC n=9, VIV n=8. Choice labels follow the deposited exact-coordinate table and do not denote transcript isoforms. d) The 46 primary genes remaining measurable under 95% dominance; blue denotes retained BY significance, orange denotes lost significance. Ecpas loses its only choice and is unmeasured rather than assigned a zero effect. The original 5,949-test family is retained, with p=1 where measurements are lost. Diagonal is equal magnitude. This sensitivity does not replace the original candidate list or constitute replication.

name: Figure_3
caption: Figure 3. Multialternative compositions and a coordinate-defined candidate. a) Every FLT–GC cluster in the joint 2,769-test family; blue denotes BY q<0.05 and the dashed line q=0.05. b) Global equal-cluster contrasts from square-root animal compositions; scaled distance is sqrt(T/2), not a percentage or the Hellinger distance between pooled group means. Exact whole-animal allocations and three-test Holm correction are as in Fig. 1. c) All 26 animals at Tcaf1 cluster 6:2:42663893:start; dots are individual animals and segments group means (FLT n=9, GC n=9, VIV n=8). Coordinates denote inclusive STAR intron ends, not exon coordinates; this minus-strand boundary shares an acceptor and varies donor-side support. The native-composition changes are descriptive components of the corrected cluster test, not separately tested alternatives. Tcaf1 passes the primary FLT–GC and FLT–VIV BY tests, but its FLT–VIV result does not survive the 95% dominance sensitivity. The selection of Tcaf1 for illustration is post hoc.

name: Figure_4
caption: Figure 4. Exact transcript context and empirical read support at Tcaf1. a) Every matching transcript for the three measured introns is shown. The minus-strand introns share genomic start 42,663,893; spans are 5,974, 22,570 and 23,000 bp. Filled endpoints mark the protein-coding Tcaf1-201/-202/-203 matches, whose exonic junction boundaries lie in the 5′ UTR. Other matches remain visible: Tcaf1-205/-206 are retained_intron and Tcaf1-208 is protein_coding_CDS_not_defined. Labels give donor→acceptor exon ranks; lines show intron spans, not complete transcripts. b) The three protein-coding matches share identical annotated coding coordinates and phases, 2,766 CDS bases and CCDS20076. Joined CDS blocks follow minus-strand transcript order; digits are GTF phases. The other matched transcripts lack a CDS annotation. These are reference relationships, not measured protein sequences. c) Every animal's 23,000-bp intron fraction and total selected counts across all three alternatives; FLT n=9, GC n=9, VIV n=8. This coverage relation is descriptive, without a new significance test. d) All 26 animals support the companion intron 6:2:42686572:42686892 with 20–169 unique reads; segments are means. Its support does not establish intron retention in a full RNA molecule. The complete audit retains 1,199/3,248 multiway junctions without exact GTF intron matches, although they passed the original STAR annotation-status filter. Tcaf1 was selected post hoc from the complete corrected family; its flight–vivarium BY result fails the 95% sensitivity and neither contrast survives half-depth BY correction. All read measurements reuse the same libraries. Flight and collection date are aliased (14 versus 17 January 2021); no causal flight, complete-isoform or protein consequence is inferred.

name: Figure_5
caption: Figure 5. Read-split repeatability and discrete discovery thresholds. a) All ten pre-existing A halves and all ten complementary B halves, obtained by subtracting A counts from the original matrix; each frozen family retains all 2,769 slots, with p=1 for failed measurements. A halves have zero BY calls; five B halves have 20–23 calls and five have zero. All 60 global comparisons retain within-half Holm significance. b) Native contrast-vector cosine between the two disjoint halves, displayed as empirical cumulative distributions for every jointly measured contrast–cluster instance and the original 43 BY-test subset. All 354 jointly measured candidate instances retain positive orientation; medians are 0.9964 for FLT–GC and 0.9933 for FLT–VIV. c) Projection onto each original native effect, divided by its squared norm, for all 751 measurable candidate half-instances and all 771 candidate animal omissions. These are descriptive repeated-instance distributions, not confidence intervals or independent samples. d) All 20 half-families and the original family at the exact minimum p=1/24,310. The curve is mH_m p_min/k for a tied minimum-p block, m=2,769; 20 floor-level tests are needed for that block to cross 0.05. The complete ordered families were checked; higher ranks can also determine a BY rejection in general. Stable direction does not establish a reliable thresholded biomarker. Halves partition the same observed reads, have dependent conditional sampling noise and share biological animals. Candidate selection is post hoc, and no threshold or family was changed.

name: Figure_6
caption: Figure 6. Comparator-specific external transport in 55 animals from three cohorts and two launches. a) Frozen RR23 multialternative panel and measurable overlap in each external cohort; the common external intersection contains 270 clusters. Gates require at least 20 selected reads and 90% dominance in every included animal. RR10 has 5 FLT and 5 GC distinct source animals but shares the RR23 launch; RRRM2 has 10 FLT and 9 GC animals from an independent launch. b) Equal-cluster scores trained using RR23 FLT–GC or FLT–VIV native-composition unit directions. Points are external FLT–GC effects; segments are conditional 95% percentile intervals from 4,000 whole-animal bootstrap draws with frozen directions. Displayed p values are exact positive-transfer tests; all four Holm-adjusted values are 1. RRRM2 allocations preserve three route/age strata (11,200 assignments); RR10 uses all 252 five-versus-five assignments. c) All ten RR10 animal scores using the FLT–GC-trained direction, centered at the overall RR10 mean for display; black segments show group means. Centering does not change the contrast. d) Tcaf1 projected effects under both frozen comparator directions and the same conditional intervals; all joint BY values are 1 across the full 3,692-slot local family. Local Holm rejection is mathematically unattainable at the available resolution and is not evidence of biological absence. The common-270-cluster sensitivity, two-cohort bootstrap intervals and every unsuccessful test are retained in Supplementary Data. No comparator was selected by external performance. Cohorts differ in sex, strain, collection and other context; exposure/date aliasing persists.

name: Figure_7
caption: Figure 7. Retrospective count-model sensitivity of frozen RR23 junction clusters. a, Standard Dirichlet–multinomial (DM) parameters were fitted to 26 animal count vectors for each of 923 clusters without using condition labels. The pooled intraclass overdispersion includes all between-animal heterogeneity; it is not a within-condition biological variance estimate. Tcaf1 is marked. b, Flight–ground exact evidence from the original square-root-composition test and pooled-covariance-whitened DM mean-logit scores. Every fixed-size animal assignment was enumerated; orange points pass BY in both complete 2,769-test families. The open circle marks Tcaf1, which overlaps other minimum-p points. Rank correlation is descriptive and does not establish independent replication. c, BY-positive contrast–cluster tests under the original analysis, DM scores, the multinomial-limit score, DM with the stricter 95% dominance gate, and DM in each of the ten original A-half count thinnings. These are separate sensitivity families; discoveries are not pooled across methods. Failed measurement gates retain p=1. All ten original A-half draws have zero local BY findings, while all 30 global DM contrasts in these A-half draws remain Holm-positive within replicate. d, Tcaf1 retains flight–ground significance with both count-score constructions, but its flight–vivarium comparison does not. All 20 full-depth DM discoveries are tied at the minimum exact p; losing one of these minimum-p tests under the stricter gate raises the minimum BY q from 0.04843 to 0.05098 without changing retained raw p values. No threshold was changed after observing this boundary. Count-model fits and score calibration are not a DRIMSeq/LeafCutter implementation, independent replication, or causal adjustment. Exact reference calibration requires animal exchangeability; condition remains confounded with collection date.

name: Figure_8
caption: Figure 8. Identification limits and measured-QC sensitivity in RR23 cerebellar junction profiles. a, The 26-animal design has identical flight and early-collection indicators and rank three for four columns; no regression can separate their coefficients. b, Primary 923-cluster Hellinger-space sensitivity: the lower bound on a remaining contrast under an assumed additive bias norm no greater than λ times the GC–VIV contrast. Solid curves use observed centroids; dotted curves allow a joint 95% bootstrap error radius across the three contrasts. The same-date GC–VIV magnitude is a hypothetical scale benchmark, not a date-effect estimate. Tipping values label the plug-in bound. c, Contrast norm ratios after simultaneous adjustment for RNA integrity number (RIN) and log2 summed library read depth, relative to the group-only model, for the 923-cluster multiway frame and 5,249 binary choices. Bars are approximate 95% percentile intervals from 10,000 joint within-arm animal bootstrap refits; they quantify measured-QC sensitivity, not causal identification. d, Multiway squared centroid distances and the inner product of FLT–VIV with GC–VIV before and after distinct-animal U-statistic correction for sampling noise. Corrected moment bars are approximate basic bootstrap intervals using analytically centered U-statistic errors; negative lower limits are retained. No inference is made from corrected cosine ratios, because most corrected bootstrap contrast Gram matrices are inadmissible. Animals, rather than reads or overlapping clusters, are the resampling unit. All analyses are retrospective and conditional on the frozen measurement frame.

name: Supplementary_Figure_1
caption: Supplementary Figure 1. All 47 primary gene candidates. a,b) The complete alphabetic list of FLT–GC genes passing joint BY correction across all 5,949 tests, with RMS effect magnitude across every measured choice assigned to the gene. These are gene-level effect summaries, not individual-animal distributions or confidence intervals. All calls have exact p=2/48,620 and joint BY q=0.04825699. Source-animal measurements, event counts and all other genes and contrasts remain in Supplementary Data 3; the 95% gate retains 45 of these 47 calls.

name: Supplementary_Figure_2
caption: Supplementary Figure 2. Dependence and read-depth diagnostics for binary choices. a) Effect-profile correlations for all 126 distinct partitions of the nine habitat controls into disjoint sets of four and five. The blue line uses the same controls in both contrasts; the dashed line is the median over disjoint partitions. Partitions reuse animals and are not independent replicates. b) All ten binomial depth thinnings of the full count matrix, with frozen binary definitions; dashed lines show unthinned effects. Target retained depth is 16,249,784 reads. All 30 global tests retain Holm significance. These diagnostics assess mathematical dependence and read sampling; they do not provide new biological replication or remove collection-date aliasing.

name: Supplementary_Figure_3
caption: Supplementary Figure 3. Gene abundance does not establish an independent junction phenotype. a) FLT–GC effects for all 1,977 jointly measurable genes; the rank correlation is descriptive and has no independent-gene significance test. b) All FLT–GC junction-association/abundance-equivalence conjunction q values, sorted separately at each margin. The conjunction p is the maximum of the exact junction p and the Welch equivalence p; BY correction covers 5,931 tests separately for each margin. No conjunction passes BY at either margin. These points summarize gene-level effects and corrected tests; they are not biological replicates. Relative abundance used the publisher-verified STAR matrix, technical-library aggregation, median-ratio normalization and log2(normalized count+0.5).

name: Supplementary_Figure_4
caption: Supplementary Figure 4. Independent-mission transport of the frozen binary profile. a) Complete measurable overlap between RR23 and RRRM2; stratum-adjusted RRRM2 effects are compared with RR23 FLT–GC effects. Spearman ρ=0.01019, with two-cohort animal-bootstrap 95% interval −0.06894 to 0.07386. b) All 19 RRRM2 animals in the three eligible strata, coloured by exposure; segments are group means. The score uses RR23-only signs and GC centering, averaged over the same 1,512 choices. Exact allocation of labels within strata yields 11,200 assignments and one-sided p=0.2525. The stratified score effect is 0.1281 pp, with frozen-weight animal-bootstrap 95% interval −0.1372 to 0.4218 pp. No common binary choice passes full-family directional Holm correction. The disputed ISS_T age-29 stratum was excluded in full.

name: Supplementary_Figure_5
caption: Supplementary Figure 5. Additional retrospective robustness checks for frozen RR23 multiway junction compositions. a) The original 43 BY-positive contrast–cluster tests (41 distinct clusters) decrease to 25 under the 95% dominance gate; all ten original A-half datasets have zero BY-positive tests. The family remains 2,769, with failed measurements assigned p=1. The 30 global comparisons across these original A-half draws all survive Holm within their replicate; this aggregate stability coexists with depth-sensitive local findings. b) Tcaf1 is valid in all ten original A-half draws, but both original local comparisons lose BY significance in these A halves. Its flight–vivarium q also rises from 0.0451 to 0.0538 under the 95% gate. All original A-half draws and the original/95% values are shown; no favorable replicate was selected. c) Observed global distances with pointwise 95% confidence-ball-derived intervals from 2,000 within-arm whole-animal bootstraps. The bootstrap centroid-error norm supplies the error radius. The intervals are approximate, not simultaneously corrected, and do not replace exact tests; nonnegative distance percentile intervals are not used to assert significance. d) Sample-size-unbiased within-group mean squared Hellinger radius, with pointwise bootstrap percentile ranges. Diagnostic Holm values follow flight–ground, flight–vivarium, ground–vivarium order. Dispersion label references recompute centroids under each assignment and require exchangeability of complete distributions; location differences invalidate an interpretation as an exact equal-dispersion test. Studentization does not guarantee small-sample validity under unequal covariance. Flight collection date (14 January 2021) is confounded with its condition versus both ground arms (17 January). These are repeated analyses of the same animals and cannot establish full isoforms, protein effects, injury, or causal flight biology. The complementary B-half results are reported separately in main Fig. 5; this panel does not summarize all 20 halves.
